claim: Let \(k\) be a field and let \(A\) be a finite-dimensional associative unital local \(k\)-algebra with \(A/J(A)\cong k\) and \(\dim_k J(A)/J(A)^2=2\). Then \(A\) has a nontrivial tensor decomposition over \(k\) if and only if there are unique integers \(m,n\ge2\), unique up to interchange, such that \(A\cong k[u,v]/(u^m,v^n)\). Equivalently, every nontrivial tensor decomposition of \(A\) is, up to order and isomorphism, \(k[t]/(t^m)\otimes_k k[s]/(s^n)\). In particular, every noncommutative split local algebra with two-dimensional cotangent space is tensor-indecomposable.
integrity: The proof is symbolic. No finite computation is used to infer the theorem. The uniqueness step invokes Sakurai's irreducible tensor-factorization theorem; the remaining cotangent-additivity and one-generator arguments are reconstructed directly.
scientific_limitations: Finite-dimensional split local algebras only; tensor products are over the ground field; cotangent dimension exactly two. No statement is made for nonsplit local algebras or cotangent dimension at least three.
title: Tensor decomposability in cotangent dimension two
